message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1.9","text":"When I said, “I would like to meet one of those who had seen him,” they immediately led me, saying, “There is someone here who has not only met him personally but also comes from the land over there—a Hebrew man named Barnabas. He also says that he himself is one of his disciples, and while sitting somewhere around here he readily tells anyone who wishes the words of his promise.” So I joined them. When I arrived, I stood with the crowd that was present and listened to his words. I perceived that he was speaking the truth, not with dialectical technique, but guilelessly and without preparation, setting out both what he had heard and what he had seen the Son of God who appeared do and say. He also furnished many witnesses to the wonders and words he recounted, including some from the very crowd that was present.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἱστορήσας αὐτὸν","chosen":"met him personally","rationale":"With a person as its object, ἱστορέω can denote visiting or becoming personally acquainted with that person."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ἐκεῖθεν γῆς ὑπάρχων","chosen":"comes from the land over there","rationale":"Preserves the geographically nonspecific deictic description of Barnabas’s origin."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ἐκείνου ὑποσχέσεως τοὺς λόγους","chosen":"the words of his promise","rationale":"Retains the source’s promise terminology without replacing it with a more familiar theological expression."},{"source_quote":"ἅ τε ἤκουσεν καὶ ἑόρακεν τὸν τοῦ θεοῦ φανέντα υἱὸν πεποιηκέναι τε καὶ εἰρηκέναι","chosen":"both what he had heard and what he had seen the Son of God who appeared do and say","rationale":"Preserves the paired acts of hearing and seeing, the Son’s appearance, and what the Son did and said."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ἐξ αὐτοῦ τοῦ παρεστῶτος ὄχλου","chosen":"including some from the very crowd that was present","rationale":"The witnesses Barnabas supplied included people drawn from the crowd then present."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.10","text":"Because the crowds were favorably disposed toward what was being said without cunning, the philosophers whose starting point was worldly education set about laughing at him and mocking him, jeering and deriding him with boundless audacity, as though they were wielding syllogisms as mighty weapons. But he, repelling their nonsense, would not join in their crafty questioning. Remaining undaunted, he continued speaking and did not desist. Once someone asked him why a gnat had come into being and, though extremely small and having six feet, also has wings, while an elephant, the largest of animals, has only four feet and is wingless. After the question, he took up the discourse that had been interrupted and, as though he had answered the question, resumed the discourse set before him from the beginning, using only this preface after each interruption: “We have only been commanded to tell you the words and wonderful deeds of the one who sent us, and instead of a logical demonstration we present to you many witnesses from among those of you who are here. I remember their forms as living images, sufficient testimonies. It is now within your power to yield or to disobey. But I will not cease telling you what benefits you, because for me silence is loss, while for you disobedience is harm. I could also furnish demonstrations in answer to your speculative questions, if you were asking in a truth-loving spirit. But now is not a suitable time to tell you the reason for the differing creation of the gnat and the elephant, when you are ignorant of the God of the universe.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οἱ ἐκ παιδείας κοσμικῆς ὁρμώμενοι φιλόσοφοι","chosen":"the philosophers whose starting point was worldly education","rationale":"The participle presents worldly education as the basis from which these philosophers proceeded."},{"source_quote":"ὁ δὲ ἀπωθούμενος αὐτῶν τὸν λῆρον οὐ συνέτρεχεν αὐτῶν τῇ πανούργῳ πεύσει","chosen":"But he, repelling their nonsense, would not join in their crafty questioning","rationale":"The wording depicts a refusal to run along with their line of questioning, not an inability to answer."},{"source_quote":"ἔλεγεν οὐκ ἀφίστατο","chosen":"he continued speaking and did not desist","rationale":"Renders both juxtaposed verbal claims rather than absorbing the second into the first."},{"source_quote":"ὡς πρὸς τὴν πεῦσιν ἀποκρινάμενος","chosen":"as though he had answered the question","rationale":"ὡς presents his resumption of the main discourse as functioning like an answer, although he does not directly explain the animals."},{"source_quote":"ὧν ἐγὼ τὰ εἴδη μέμνημαι ὡς ἐμψύχους εἰκόνας ἱκανὰς μαρτυρίας","chosen":"I remember their forms as living images, sufficient testimonies","rationale":"Preserves the unusual progression from remembered forms to living images and sufficient testimonies."},{"source_quote":"τῶν εἰκαίων ὑμῶν προβλημάτων","chosen":"your speculative questions","rationale":"εἰκαῖος characterizes the proposed problems as conjectural or based on probability."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς τῶν ὅλων ἀγνοοῦσι θεόν","chosen":"when you are ignorant of the God of the universe","rationale":"The participle characterizes the hearers, while τῶν ὅλων identifies God in relation to the totality of things."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.11","text":"As he was saying these things, they let loose disorderly laughter as though by agreement, trying to silence him and leave him at a loss, as if he were some demon-possessed barbarian. When I saw this, I was seized—I do not know how—with zeal and pious indignation, and could no longer endure remaining silent. Instead, I cried out boldly: “God had good reason to make his will incomprehensible to you, since he foresaw that you were unworthy, as is apparent from the things through which he now gives assurance to those who possess a discerning mind. For now heralds of his will have been sent out, not professing grammatical skill but disclosing his will in simple and guileless words, so that absolutely anyone who hears can understand what is said, and not with some grudging polish unwilling to make itself available to everyone. Yet you are here, besides failing to understand what benefits you, laughing to your own harm at the truth that made its home among barbarians for your condemnation. Although it has now visited you as well, you do not wish to receive it as a guest, because of your licentiousness and the plainness of its words, lest you be exposed as lovers of words to no purpose and not philosophers who love truth. How long, then, will you go on learning to talk, when you do not know how to speak well? For many utterances from you are not worth one reasoned statement. What, then, will your Greek multitude say, having become one soul, if there really is to be a judgment, as this man says? ‘Why, O God, did you not proclaim your will to us?’ Will you not most certainly hear—if indeed you are deemed worthy of an answer—the following? ‘Knowing before the foundation of the world every choice that would be made, I secretly met each person beforehand according to what that person deserved. Wishing to assure those who have taken refuge with me of this very fact—that matters stand so—and of why, from the beginning, in earlier generations, I did not allow my will to be proclaimed publicly, I have now, near the end of life, sent heralds of my purpose. They are laughed at and, while being abused, are mocked by those who are unwilling to receive any benefit and who have vehemently rejected my friendship. Oh, what great injustice! The heralds are in danger to the point of murder, and that at the hands of the very men being called to salvation.’”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὡς βάρβαρόν τινα δαιμονῶντα","chosen":"as if he were some demon-possessed barbarian","rationale":"δαιμονάω can describe possession by a demon or the madness attributed to such possession; the explicit demonic characterization is retained."},{"source_quote":"ἀναξίους προιδὼν ὡς ἐξ ὧν νῦν τοὺς κριτικὸν νοῦν ἔχοντας πληροφορῶν φαίνεται","chosen":"since he foresaw that you were unworthy, as is apparent from the things through which he now gives assurance to those who possess a discerning mind","rationale":"This takes God as the understood subject of πληροφορῶν and ἐξ ὧν as identifying the grounds or means from which his judgment becomes apparent."},{"source_quote":"ὡς πάνθ’ ὁντιναοῦν ἀκούσαντα νοεῖν τὰ λεγόμενα","chosen":"so that absolutely anyone who hears can understand what is said","rationale":"The wording emphasizes that the heralds’ plain speech is accessible to anyone whatsoever."},{"source_quote":"καὶ οὐ μετὰ ξέσεώς τινος φθονερᾶς, παρέχειν πᾶσιν ἑαυτὴν μὴ βουλομένης","chosen":"and not with some grudging polish unwilling to make itself available to everyone","rationale":"ξέσις denotes polishing or refinement of expression, personified here as grudgingly withholding itself from general access."},{"source_quote":"τὴν εἰς τὴν ὑμετέραν καταδίκην ἐν βαρβάροις πολιτευσαμένην ἀλήθειαν","chosen":"the truth that made its home among barbarians for your condemnation","rationale":"πολιτεύομαι personifies truth as dwelling or conducting its life among a people."},{"source_quote":"εἰκῇ φιλόλογοί ἐστε καὶ οὐ φιλαληθεῖς φιλόσοφοι","chosen":"lovers of words to no purpose and not philosophers who love truth","rationale":"Preserves the contrast and wordplay between devotion to words and devotion to truth."},{"source_quote":"πολλὰ γὰρ παρ’ ὑμῶν ῥήματα ἑνὸς οὐκ ἄξια λόγου","chosen":"For many utterances from you are not worth one reasoned statement","rationale":"Distinguishes the many individual utterances from one meaningful or reasoned λόγος."},{"source_quote":"ἑκάστῳ πρὸς τὸ αὐτοῦ ἄξιον λανθανόντως προαπήντησα","chosen":"I secretly met each person beforehand according to what that person deserved","rationale":"Retains the metaphor of meeting in advance and relates that hidden prior encounter to each person’s deserts."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τῷ τέλει τοῦ βίου","chosen":"near the end of life","rationale":"Preserves the explicit βίου without substituting the unsupplied and more familiar expressions “end of the world” or “end of the age.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὡς ἐξ ὧν νῦν τοὺς κριτικὸν νοῦν ἔχοντας πληροφορῶν φαίνεται","issue":"The syntax is compressed, and the precise attachment and force of ὡς ἐξ ὧν are uncertain. The translation understands the phrase as giving evidence or grounds by which God’s prior judgment becomes apparent, but other construals are possible.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"1.12","text":"“‘This injustice being done against my heralds would have been done against everyone from the beginning, if the unworthy had been called to salvation from the beginning. For what is now being done unjustly by them serves as a defense of my just providence: I rightly did not wish from the beginning to expose publicly and fruitlessly to abuse the message worthy of honor. Rather, I resolved that it should be kept silent as something precious—not from those who were worthy from the beginning, to whom I did impart it, but from these and others like them, who, as you see, are unworthy, who hate me and are unwilling to love themselves.’ And now at least, stop laughing at this man and question me concerning what he proclaims; or let anyone who wishes answer me while I question him. Do not bark like wanton dogs, shutting the ears of those who wish to be saved with disorderly noise. You unjust people, hateful to God, who divert the reasoning that saves into unbelief—how can you obtain forgiveness when you insult the one who professes to tell you about the divinity of God? And this is a man whom, even if he were saying nothing true, you ought to have welcomed because of his good intention toward you.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ἂν εἰς πάντας ἐγίνετο","chosen":"would have been done against everyone from the beginning","rationale":"The rendering leaves πάντας general because its precise referent—every person or all the heralds—is not expressed."},{"source_quote":"εἰς ἀπολογίαν τῆς ἐμῆς δικαίας γίνεται προνοίας","chosen":"serves as a defense of my just providence","rationale":"ἀπολογία denotes a defense or vindication; the heralds’ present mistreatment is said to vindicate the earlier withholding."},{"source_quote":"τὸν τιμῆς ἄξιον λόγον","chosen":"the message worthy of honor","rationale":"λόγος here denotes the content being proclaimed; “message” avoids importing a personified or canonical sense."},{"source_quote":"ἀλλὰ σιγᾶσθαι αὐτὸν ὡς τίμιον ἐβουλευσάμην","chosen":"Rather, I resolved that it should be kept silent as something precious","rationale":"The passive infinitive depicts the message as withheld, while τίμιος describes its precious or honored status."},{"source_quote":"καὶ νῦν γε παρέντες· γελᾶν τὸν ἄνδρα τοῦτον","chosen":"And now at least, stop laughing at this man","rationale":"Despite the supplied punctuation after παρέντες, the participle is understood with γελᾶν in the sense of leaving off or ceasing an action."},{"source_quote":"μύοντες τῶν σώζεσθαι θελόντων τὰς ἀκοάς","chosen":"shutting the ears of those who wish to be saved","rationale":"Preserves the physical image of closing the hearers’ ears rather than generalizing it as interference."},{"source_quote":"θεοστυγεῖς","chosen":"hateful to God","rationale":"The adjective can be understood as “hated by God” or “hateful to God”; the latter preserves its condemnatory force without turning it into the distinct active claim “haters of God.”"},{"source_quote":"τὸν σώζοντα λογισμὸν εἰς ἀπιστίαν ἀπασχολοῦντες","chosen":"who divert the reasoning that saves into unbelief","rationale":"ἀπασχολέω conveys occupying or drawing something aside; the rendering preserves both the reasoning’s saving function and its diversion toward unbelief."},{"source_quote":"τὴν θειότητα τοῦ θεοῦ","chosen":"the divinity of God","rationale":"Retains the source’s explicit and somewhat tautological wording without expanding it into a later doctrinal formula."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ἂν εἰς πάντας ἐγίνετο","issue":"The masculine plural πάντας has no explicit local referent. It may mean that the injustice would have been directed against everyone, or against all the heralds; the translation retains the broader wording.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
